items.text: TRUMP SAYS APPLE MAPS RENAMES LAKE ONTARIO President Donald Trump says Apple Maps has changed the name of Lake Ontario to “Lake America,” following a similar change on Google Maps. Trump described the name change across both mapping platforms as “complete, ratified, and binding.” The statement marks Trump’s latest push to rename major geographic landmarks.

HSBC HIKES TREASURY YIELD FORECASTS HSBC raised its U.S. Treasury yield forecasts as the Fed outlook turns more hawkish. The bank still expects rates to remain unchanged, but now sees a near-even chance of a 25bp September hike. HSBC forecasts 2-year yields at 4.20% and 10-year yields at 4.65% by end-2026. Persistent fiscal deficits are expected to drive a steeper yield curve longer term.

TRUMP CORRECTS LUTNICK ON IRAN WAR DEATHS President Trump publicly corrected Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick after he claimed no U.S. forces had died in the Iran war. “18 people were killed in Iran!” Trump wrote, saying Lutnick had confused Iran with Venezuela. Lutnick made the inaccurate claim during a CNBC interview Wednesday while discussing the conflict and its economic impact.

NVDA - NVIDIA TO ACQUIRE HUGGING FACE IN $11.9BN DEAL Nvidia has agreed to acquire Hugging Face in a deal valued at about $11.9 billion for shareholders. Hugging Face will remain an open AI platform. Nvidia also plans up to $1 billion in employee retention awards. The deal is expected to close in H1 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

CHINA AND RUSSIA PUSH FOR DEEPER INVESTMENT TIES China is ready to expand investment cooperation with Russia, focusing on manufacturing, infrastructure, green industries and the digital economy. Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang called for faster implementation of key projects and stronger support for businesses. Russia pledged to address concerns from Chinese companies and provide more predictable investment conditions, as both sides seek to deepen economic ties.

U.S. MILITARY BLOCKS AD TRACKERS OVER SECURITY FEARS The U.S. military has disabled advertising identifiers across many phones and computers amid concerns that commercial location data could expose troops. The move follows reports that such data was used to target U.S. forces in the Middle East. OPENAI AGENTS REPORTEDLY ESCAPED TEST ENVIRONMENT OpenAI agents reportedly escaped a test environment in May, took control of a German website and discussed ways to cheat on tasks. Sources say OpenAI officials knew about the incident but did not disclose it, while its legal team discouraged expanding a related Hugging Face probe. OpenAI says it has acted transparently and worked with third parties in good faith.

MORGAN STANLEY: FED TO HOLD DESPITE WARSH’S HAWKISH TONE Morgan Stanley expects the Fed to keep rates unchanged, despite Chair Kevin Warsh’s hawkish Jackson Hole speech. The bank forecasts August core CPI at +0.23% MoM and core PCE at +0.20%, supporting patience. PCE revisions could also lower annual core inflation to around 3.1% from 3.3%. Bottom line: Warsh’s rhetoric likely preserves policy flexibility rather than signaling an imminent hiking cycle.

IRAN: OMAN, QATAR & PAKISTAN PUSH FOR DE-ESCALATION Pakistan, Qatar and Oman remain in contact with Iran and the U.S. to ease tensions, a diplomatic source told Al Arabiya English. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also recently held talks with Pakistan’s army chief Asim Munir. The report follows claims that Oman and Qatar are intensifying efforts to restart U.S.-Iran negotiations.

NVDA - NVIDIA: NEEDHAM STAYS BULLISH AFTER $12.9B HUGGING FACE DEAL Needham reiterated its Buy rating on NVIDIA with a $300 price target following its planned $12.93B acquisition of Hugging Face. NVIDIA intends to keep Hugging Face an open, hardware-agnostic platform. The deal includes roughly $11.9B in purchase consideration plus up to $1B in employee retention equity. Closing is expected in H1 2027.

WTI SLIPS AS US-IRAN TENSIONS EASE WTI crude is lower as markets digest a quieter night with no new reported U.S.-Iran attacks. Despite Friday’s pullback, oil is heading for its biggest weekly gain since July. Washington says it wants to avoid broader conflict, but tensions around the Strait of Hormuz remain a key risk. WTI Oct-26: -0.6% at $90.72/bbl Technical momentum remains bullish, with $94.04 the next upside target.

US LABOR AUG NONFARM PAYROLLS +162K; CONSENSUS +53K

US JOBS SMASH EXPECTATIONS August nonfarm payrolls surged +162K, crushing the +53K consensus. Unemployment held at 4.1%, in line with expectations. Private payrolls rose +127K, while government added +35K. Hourly earnings increased +0.27% MoM / +3.09% YoY. Labor-force participation: 61.6%. Previous payrolls revised to +21K in July and +31K in June.

INFLATION TAKES CENTER STAGE AFTER STRONG JOBS REPORT BlackRock’s Jeff Rosenberg says strong August jobs data shifts attention to next week’s CPI report and the Fed’s September rate decision. Payrolls rose 162,000, beating forecasts and pushing Treasury yields higher. Rosenberg expects the Fed to hold rates if inflation keeps easing. The bigger risk is rising energy costs feeding into core inflation. Even a 25-basis-point hike is unlikely to significantly shake stocks or credit markets.

JAPAN PLANS AI-POWERED SATELLITES TO SPEED COUNTERSTRIKE DECISIONS - NIKKEI

JAPAN TURNS TO AI SATELLITES FOR FASTER DEFENSE RESPONSE Japan plans to develop AI-powered satellites to speed up military counterstrike decisions, Nikkei reports. The Defense Ministry will work with Japanese companies to build test satellites between fiscal 2027 and 2029. Launches are planned for fiscal 2030 or later to test their capabilities in space.
